title: Walking home with Louis Armstrong
summary: Cootie, living at Braud's house, walked home with Louis Armstrong from the Savoy after his Cotton Club job, one of his biggest thrills.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: I'll be darned. Fancy that. That is strange, isn't it? Well, listen, say I just remembered that when you and I talked before, talking about Wellman Braud, just go back to when you came up, you know, with Alonzo. Then you told me before that you stayed at Braud's house, and so did Louis, because they were friends. And you got to walk to the Savoy every night with Louis and it was a terrific kick for you.

Yeah, I got that chance. Now, we were playing at the Cotton Club, and Louis was playing at the Savoy, and when we would get off, I would go by the Savoy, and walk home with Louis, and talk with Louis.
Yeah. And that was one of the biggest thrills I had in my life.
Well, was Louis staying at Brough's house?
How about that. And you would walk back together.
But you were younger than he was, though.
So this was a big privilege for you, really, huh?
How about that. What would you do, just go there and he knew you were waiting for him to get off and so on?
How about that. Did he ever say anything? Did he ever -- was he ever helpful about the horn? Or you didn't

No. Well, I would stand up there and listen to him blow. And there would be this amaze out of me that he could blow that trumpet like that. Wait till he got off. And I was asking him was he going home, could I walk home with him. Then he'd tell me yes, and I'd walk home with him.
That's terrific, isn't it? Did you -- you stayed good friends?
Yeah. And a funny man, too, wasn't he, Cootie?
He had a great -- I mean, he loved -- he liked to tell jokes and things, didn't he?
He liked to laugh, didn't he?
Yeah. Loved to tell jokes. The only thing I would be interested in was listening to him blow that horn.
You didn't care about the jokes.
